original_question: For the Tannakian quotient groups pi_1^(r)(X) attached to stratified vector bundles on a connected smooth projective curve X over the algebraic closure of a finite field, how much of the curve X is determined by the collection of groups pi_1^(r)(X)?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, as sharpened by Proposition 1.2: whether a connected smooth projective curve over an algebraic closure of a finite field is determined, up to Frobenius twist, by the Tannakian quotient groups attached to its stratified vector bundles.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main objects of the paper: the Tannakian quotient groups pi_1^(r)(X), stratified vector bundles, and the setting of a connected smooth projective curve over the algebraic closure of a finite field. It also captures the paper's central anabelian/Torelli-style theme: recovering the curve from these groups.
missing_details: The paper's question is comparative: it concerns two curves X and Y, not just one curve X in isolation.
The quantifier over ranks must be explicit: the comparison is for every integer r >= 1.

The notation pi_1^(r)(X) should be defined stand-alone as the Tannaka group of the tensor subcategory generated by stratified vector bundles of rank at most r (or the corresponding rank-r Tannakian quotient, as in the paper's setup).
The comparison is between these objects as affine group schemes/Tannakian quotients over k, not merely as abstract groups.
The paper-faithful conclusion is not literal recovery of X without qualification: the natural ambiguity coming from Frobenius twist must be built into the statement.
Accordingly, the conclusion should say that X and Y are isomorphic up to an iterate of Frobenius, i.e. Y is isomorphic to X^(n) for some integer n.
The base field should be named explicitly as k = \bar{\mathbf{F}}_q (equivalently an algebraic closure of a finite field, hence characteristic p > 0).

If one wants the question to be fully self-contained, one should also indicate that a neutral fiber functor/base point is fixed to define the Tannakian groups, though the resulting determination problem is independent of that choice up to the usual equivalence.
refined_question: Let k = \bar{\mathbf{F}}_q be an algebraic closure of a finite field, and let X and Y be connected smooth projective curves over k. For each integer r >= 1, let pi_1^(r)(X) (resp. pi_1^(r)(Y)) denote the rank-r Tannakian quotient attached to the neutral Tannakian category of stratified vector bundles on X (resp. Y). If pi_1^(r)(X) is isomorphic to pi_1^(r)(Y) for every r >= 1, must X and Y be isomorphic up to Frobenius twist; equivalently, does there exist an integer n such that Y is k-isomorphic to X^(n)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as reformulated in Proposition 1.2, does the full Tannakian data of stratified bundles determine a connected smooth projective curve over \bar{\mathbf{F}}_q only up to its Frobenius orbit?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's main conjectural reconstruction problem, but it is not yet paper-faithful as a stand-alone research question. The crucial missing point is the Frobenius ambiguity: in the paper's formulation, one should not ask whether the groups determine X absolutely, but whether they determine X up to Frobenius twist. The nearby Proposition 1.2 supplies the sharper reformulation to use, and Theorem 1.3 provides supporting context for why this is the right formulation. So the refined question above stays close to your draft while restoring the exact comparison setup, the universal quantifier over r, the definition-level role of the Tannakian quotients, and the paper-critical Frobenius qualification.
